PANCHAYAT

EVOLUTION OF PANCHAYAT

Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, 1957

  • Recommendation: 3-tier Panchayati Raj System
  1. 1. Gram Panchayat - Village level
  2. 2. Panchayat Samiti - Block level
  3. 3. Zila Parishad - District level
  • Rajasthan - 1st state to implement Panchayati Raj at Nagaur, on 2nd October 1959 followed by Andhra Pradesh on October 11, 1959.

Ashok Mehta Committee, 1977

  • Proposed: 2-tier Panchayati Raj System
  1. 1. Zila Parishad (main unit)
  2. 2. Mandal Panchayat

G.V.K Rao Committee, 1985

  • Reviewed the working of Constitution in relation to the working of the Panchayats and Municipalities.
  • Proposed Zila Parishad to act as the Nodal agency for development.

L.M. Singhvi Committee, 1986

  • 1st to recommend constitutional status for PRIs that they should constitutionally recognised, protected, and preserved.
  • Advocated for financial autonomy of Panchayats.
  • It also emphasised the importance of the Gram Sabha and called it the embodiment of direct democracy.
  • Nyaya Panchayats should be established for a cluster of villages.

Thungon Committee, 1988

Gadgil Committee, 1988

  • To examine the role of Panchayati Raj Institutions in rural development.
  • Members at all three levels should be directly elected.
  • Term should be fixed at 5 years.
  • Reservation for SC, ST and Women

73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992

  • Made it mandatory to establish Panchayati Raj institutions by inserting—
  • Part IX, Article: 243-243O
  • Added Schedule 11 that contains 29 functional items.
  • Enforced on 24th April, 1993 (that's why this day is celebrated as Panchayati Raj Day).
  • Then PM: P. V. Narasimha Rao.

Articles related to Panchayat

Article 243: Definition

  • "Gram Sabha" means a body consisting of persons registered in electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.

Article 243A: Gram Sabha

  • A Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at village level as the Legislature of State may, by law, provide.

Article 243B: Constitution of Panchayats

  • There shall be constituted in every state, Panchayat at village, intermediate, and district level i.e.,
  1. 1. Constitution of 3-tier Panchayati Raj System
  2. 2. Panchayat at intermediate level, not to be constituted in a state having a population, not exceeding 20 lakhs

Article 243C: Composition of Panchayats

(1) All seats in Panchayat shall be filled by persons chosen by direct election.

(2) The Chairperson of a Panchayat at village level shall be elected in such manner as the Legislature of a state may, by law, provide and at intermediate and district level through an indirect election.

Article 243D: Reservation of Seats

(1) Seats are reserved for SC/ST in proportion of their population

(2) 1/3rd seats are reserved for women.

Article 243E: Duration of Panchayats, etc.

(1) Duration of Panchayats: A 5-year term, unless dissolved earlier by applicable laws.

(3) Election Time

  • (a) Before the end of its 5 year term.
  • (b) Dissolution: If Panchayat is dissolved before its term ends, election must be held within 6 months of dissolution date. (If remaining term is less than 6 months, election is not mandatory).

(4) Term of Reconstitution: Panchayat formed after early dissolution will serve only for the remainder of original term.

Example:

  • 1 Jan 2020 — 1 Jan 2025
  • 20 Nov 2024: Less than 6 months → (Election not mandatory) (Dissolution)
  • 1 Jan 2024: More than 6 months → (Election Mandatory) (Dissolution)
  • Dissolving power: Zila Parishad → New Panchayat formed will serve remainder of the term (1 year in this case)

Article 243F: Disqualifications of Membership

(1) Law made by State legislature can cause disqualification.

(a) A person convicted of a certain offense or declared insolvent may be disqualified from being a Panchayat member if they are disqualified by law related to state elections.

  • He cannot be disqualified if he is less than 25 years (minimum required age 21 years)

(b) Disqualification is decided by such authority as determined by State Legislature.

High Court deals with the election disputes of MP/MLAs

Article 243G: Power, Authority, and Responsibilities of Panchayats

  • State legislature, by law, endow, the Panchayat with such powers an authority that may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government.

Article 243H: Power to Impose Taxes

  • State legislature can authorise the Panchayat- To levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls, and fees, grant-in-aids, ensuring proper financial management.

Article 243I: Constitution of Finance Commission by Governor to review financial position

  • Government shall lay the recommendation of Commission before the State Legislature.

Article 243J: Audit of Accounts of Panchayats

Article 243K: Election to the Panchayats

(1) All elections of Panchayat shall be conducted by State Election Commission.

  • The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.

(2) The conditions of service and tenure of office of State Election Commissioner are determined by the Governor. He can be removed from his office in the same manner as the judge of a High Court.

Article 243L: Application to Union Territories

  • Provisions of Part IX, of Constitution, which deals with Panchayats, shall apply to UTs with certain modification and exceptions.

Article 243M: Part not to Apply to Certain Areas

(1) Exclusion of certain areas like tribal regions and some North-Eastern states from the Panchayat system to respect their unique governance traditions, and local customs. However, provisions can be extended to these areas with necessary modification through specific laws.

The PESA Act, 1996.
The Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, extends these provisions of Part IX of the Indian Constitution, to the Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule Areas) of India.

(2) Nothing in this part shall apply to:

  • (a) Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram (Panchayati Raj system do not exist here)
  • (b) Hill areas of Manipur (District Council exist here)
Delhi is the only UT where provisions of the Panchayats are not applicable.

Article 243N: Continuance of Existing laws and Panchayats

Article 243N ensures a smooth transition to the new Panchayati Raj System by allowing all law to remain temporarily valid, while the State makes necessary changes to comply with updated constitutional framework.

Article 243O: Bar to Interference by Courts in Electoral Matters

(a) Courts cannot interfere in the process of defining Panchayat constituencies, or assigning seats.

MUNICIPALITIES

  • Introduced through: 74th CA, 1992
  • → Part IXA, Art 243P-243ZG
  • → Added 12th Schedule that contains 18 functional items
  • First Municipal Corporation was set up in Madras in 1687-1688
  • 1870: Lord Mayo presented resolution of Financial Decentralisation
  • Ripon's resolution of 1882 is known as "Magna Carta of Local Self-Government".
  • Municipal Corporation in Calcutta & Bombay were set up in: 1726
Ripon is also known as "Father of Local Self-Government"

There are 8 types of Urban Local Government

  • → Municipal Corporation
  • → Municipality
  • → Notified Area Committee
  • → Cantonment Board (Military)
  • → Township
  • → Town Area Committee
  • → Port Trust
  • → Special Purpose Agency

3 Types of Municipalities

  • Nagar Panchayat: For a Transitional Area
  • Municipal Council: For a small urban Area
  • Municipal Corporation: For a larger urban Area
All seats are filled through direct elections.
Elections conducted by: State Election Commission

Part IXB – The Co-operative Societies - (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT)

  • Inserted by: 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.
  • Grants constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies.
  • Provisions relating to the formation, regulation, and functioning of Co-operative societies.
